'''Thabo Patrick Sefolosha''' ({{IPAc-en|ˈ|t|ɑː|b|oʊ|_|ˌ|s|ɛ|f|ə|ˈ|l|oʊ|ʃ|ə}}; born 2 May 1984) is a Swiss former professional [[basketball]] player. He played in the [[National Basketball Association]] (NBA), the [[Turkish Basketball League]], [[LNB Pro A]], and [[Lega Basket Serie A]]. In 2006, Sefolosha became the first player from Switzerland to play in the NBA, and in 2013, he was labelled the best Swiss basketball player of all time by Swiss newspaper [[Freiburger Nachrichten]].<ref>[http://www.freiburger-nachrichten.ch/sport-basketball/der-neue-nati-trainer-petar-aleksic-soll-das-unmoegliche-moeglich-machen Der neue Nati-Trainer Petar Aleksic soll das Unmögliche möglich machen] {{in lang|de}}</ref>

==Early life==
Sefolosha was born on 2 May 1984 in [[Vevey]], Switzerland to Patrick Sefolosha, a South African musician, and [[Christine Sefolosha]] (née Beck), a Swiss artist. Sefolosha speaks French, Italian, and English.<ref name="Bulls article">"[http://www.nba.com/bulls/news/sefolosha_feature_060914.html Thabo Sefolosha: Coming to America]." NBA: September 14, 2006.</ref>

==Professional career==

===Early years (2001–2006)===
Sefolosha was invited to join the junior Swiss national basketball team, and at age 17, he began a professional career with [[Vevey Riviera Basket]], in Switzerland's top domestic league.<ref name="Bulls article"/> On a team trip to France, Sefolosha was approached by a French talent scout to play with [[Élan Chalon]] in the premier pro league in France.<ref name="Bulls article"/>

Sefolosha spent his first year in [[Chalon-sur-Saône]] playing with the junior under-21 squad, which traveled alongside the senior club. The following year (2002–03), Sefolosha earned a rotation spot on the senior club, where he played 30 games and averaged 4.0 [[Points per game|points]], 3.5 [[Rebound (basketball)|rebounds]] and 1.0 [[Assist (basketball)|assists]] per game.<ref name="Bulls article"/>

The following season, Sefolosha earned a starting spot on the senior team, which he helped lead to a third-place finish in the French league and his team advanced to the [[playoffs]] semifinals. During the season, Sefolosha averaged 9.4 points, 7.0 rebounds, and 1.0 [[Steal (basketball)|steal]] in 30.7 minutes per game.<ref name="Bulls article"/>

Before the start of his fourth season with Élan Chalon, a contract dispute between Sefolosha and the team arose. Sefolosha's agent and the team president could not reach an agreement on a new contract, so Sefolosha signed with Italian team [[Pallacanestro Biella|Angelico Biella]]. "Last summer, I had the chance to re-negotiate my contract with the club. We were supposed to reach an agreement, but when my agent and the president started talking, they couldn't agree on a contract. They wanted to keep me, but at the same time I had this offer from Italy. That's when I decided that the best thing for my career was to play in Biella. Yes, there was a little bit of trouble, but in the end it was OK."<ref name="HoopsHype">[http://www.hoopshype.com/interviews/sefolosha_sierra.htm HoopsHype interview with Sefolosha] URL last accessed September 27, 2006</ref>

===Chicago Bulls (2006–2009)===
Sefolosha was taken with the 13th pick of the [[2006 NBA draft]] by the [[Philadelphia 76ers]] and promptly traded to the [[Chicago Bulls]] for the 16th pick ([[Rodney Carney]]), and cash considerations.<ref name="ESPN Draft">[https://www.espn.com/nba/draft2006/news/story?id=2503390 ESPN article on the 2006 NBA Draft] URL last accessed September 27, 2006</ref> In an article on Bulls.com, Sefolosha was quoted saying "I was certainly surprised (at the draft) when someone came up and said that I was the next to be picked. I thought maybe he had made a mistake or something. But a few minutes later he came back and told me that not only was I going to be picked, but that I was going to be traded to Chicago, which really got me excited."<ref name="Bulls article"/>

Bulls head coach [[Scott Skiles]] cited that Sefolosha's wingspan and past pro basketball experience as reasons why the Bulls were interested in him. "Thabo's got great physical gifts that, frankly, a lot of guys in the league just don't have. He's got tremendous length and has really quick hands, he grabs your attention whenever you watch him play. It's easy to see that he knows what he's doing out there. You can tell he likes to play defense, too. He's eager to get after it."<ref name="Bulls article"/>

After the NBA summer leagues finished, [[ESPN]] asked several NBA talent scouts and executives to rank the summer league players, and Sefolosha scored high. "He excelled at just about everything," reported one of the professionals. "Thabo Sefolosha showed that he's going to be able to step in right away and contribute to the Bulls."<ref name="Bulls article"/>

===Oklahoma City Thunder (2009–2014)===
[[File:Thabo Sefolosha Thunder.jpg|thumb|upright|Sefolosha in 2011|left]]
On 19 February 2009, the trade deadline, Sefolosha was traded by the Bulls to the [[Oklahoma City Thunder]] for Denver's [[2009 NBA draft|2009 first-round draft]] pick, which Chicago used to draft [[Taj Gibson]].<ref>{{cite web |url=http://www.nba.com/thunder/news/aquirethabo_090219.html |title=Thunder Acquires Thabo Sefolosha |work=NBA.com |date=February 19, 2009 |access-date=March 9, 2013}}</ref> Sefolosha was selected to the [[All-NBA Defensive Team|All-NBA Defensive Second Team]] for the [[2009–10 NBA season]].{{fact|date=March 2025}}

In October 2011, during the [[2011 NBA lockout]], Sefolosha signed with [[Fenerbahçe Ülker]] in Turkey, but only for [[Euroleague]] matches. His deal had an out-clause that allowed him to return to Oklahoma City at the end of the lockout.<ref>{{Cite news |url=https://archive.boston.com/sports/basketball/articles/2011/10/12/oklahoma_citys_sefolosha_signs_with_turkish_club/ |title=Thabo Sefolosha signs With a Turkish Club |date=October 12, 2011 |access-date=March 9, 2013|newspaper=Boston.com }}</ref> He played seven games with Fenerbahçe Ülker during the [[Fenerbahçe Ülker Euroleague 2011–12|2011–12 Euroleague season]].

In 2012, Sefolosha and the Thunder reached the NBA Finals, but were defeated by the [[Miami Heat]] in five games.{{fact|date=March 2025}}

Sefolosha was a permanent member of the starting five, including in the Thunder's run to the finals. Starting as shooting guard, before [[James Harden]] (who came off the bench), Sefolosha received major playing time mainly due to his defensive abilities.{{fact|date=March 2025}}

===Atlanta Hawks (2014–2017)===
[[File:Thabo Sefolosha (cropped).jpg|thumb|Sefolosha in 2016]]
On 15 July 2014, Sefolosha was acquired by the [[Atlanta Hawks]] in a sign-and-trade deal, along with rights to [[Giorgos Printezis]], in exchange for the rights to [[Sofoklis Schortsanitis]].<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.nba.com/hawks/news/hawks-acquire-thabo-sefolosha-sign-trade-transaction|title=Hawks Acquire Thabo Sefolosha in Sign-And-Trade Transaction|work=Atlanta Hawks|access-date=April 8, 2015}}</ref>

On 31 January 2015, Sefolosha was ruled out for six to eight weeks with a strained right calf.<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.nba.com/hawks/thabo-sefolosha-expected-miss-6-8-weeks|title=Thabo Sefolosha Expected To Miss 6-8 Weeks|work=Atlanta Hawks|access-date=April 8, 2015}}</ref> On April 9, he was ruled out for the rest of the regular season due to a fractured tibia suffered while being arrested by members of the [[New York City Police Department]].<ref>{{cite news|last1=Dwyer|first1=Kelly|title=Thabo Sefolosha out for season following an altercation with police|url=https://sports.yahoo.com/blogs/nba-ball-dont-lie/reports--thabo-sefolosha-out-for-season-following-an-altercation-with-police-215727447.html|access-date=October 10, 2015|work=Yahoo! Sports|date=April 9, 2015}}</ref>

===Utah Jazz (2017–2019)===
On 18 July 2017, Sefolosha signed a multi-year deal with the [[Utah Jazz]].<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.nba.com/jazz/news/jazz-sign-thabo-sefolosha|title=Jazz Sign Thabo Sefolosha|work=NBA.com|date=July 18, 2017|access-date=July 18, 2017}}</ref>

On 12 January 2018, in Utah's 99–88 loss to the [[Charlotte Hornets]], Sefolosha suffered a right [[Medial collateral ligament|MCL]] injury.<ref>{{cite web|last=Jones|first=Tony|url=https://www.sltrib.com/sports/jazz/2018/01/13/sources-thabo-sefolosha-may-be-out-for-season-in-another-blow-to-jazzs-season/|title=Sources: Thabo Sefolosha may be out for season in another blow to Jazz's season|work=sltrib.com|date=January 13, 2018|access-date=January 15, 2018}}</ref> He underwent season-ending surgery five days later.<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.nba.com/article/2018/01/17/utah-jazz-thabo-sefolosha-undergoes-knee-surgery|title=Utah Jazz forward Thabo Sefolosha undergoes knee surgery|work=NBA.com|date=January 17, 2018|access-date=April 3, 2018}}</ref> On 3 April, Sefolosha was suspended without pay for five games for violating the terms of the NBA/NBPA Anti-Drug Program.<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.nba.com/article/2018/04/03/mavericks-nerlens-noel-jazz-thabo-sefolosha-suspended-official-release|title=Mavericks' Nerlens Noel, Jazz's Thabo Sefolosha suspended for violating anti-drug program|work=NBA.com|date=April 3, 2018|access-date=April 3, 2018}}</ref>

===Houston Rockets (2019–2020)===
On 23 September 2019, Sefolosha signed a one-year deal with the [[Houston Rockets]].<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.chron.com/sports/rockets/article/Rockets-to-sign-Thabo-Sefolosha-14455239.php|title=Rockets to sign Thabo Sefolosha|work=chron.com|date=September 20, 2019|access-date=September 20, 2019}}</ref><ref>{{cite web|title=Rockets Sign Free Agent Thabo Sefolosha|url=https://www.nba.com/rockets/news/rockets-sign-free-agent-thabo-sefolosha|website=NBA.com|access-date=September 24, 2019|date=September 23, 2019}}</ref>

=== Initial retirement ===
Sefolosha announced his retirement from professional basketball on 31 March 2021.<ref>{{Cite web|title=Thabo Sefolosha retires after 14 NBA seasons|url=https://supersport.com/general/xtra/news/210331_Thabo_Sefolosha_retires_after_14_NBA_seasons|access-date=2021-05-03|website=supersport.com|language=en}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web|title=Report: Former Bull Thabo Sefolosha retires|url=https://www.nbcsports.com/chicago/bulls/report-former-bulls-guard-thabo-sefolosha-retires|access-date=2021-05-03|website=RSN|language=en}}</ref>

===Vevey Riviera Basket (2023)===
Despite announcing his retirement two years prior, Sefolosha signed with the Swiss team [[Vevey Riviera Basket]] on 26 January 2023,<ref>{{cite web|url=https://basketnews.com/news-184359-thabo-sefolosha-signs-with-a-team-in-switzerland.html|title=Thabo Sefolosha signs with a team in Switzerland|publisher=BasketNews.com|date=January 26, 2023|accessdate=January 26, 2023}}</ref> returning to the club where he first played professionally.

==Personal life==
On 8 April 2015, Sefolosha and teammate [[Pero Antić]] were arrested outside a nightclub in New York City for allegedly interfering with police after [[Chris Copeland]] of the [[Indiana Pacers]] was stabbed in the abdomen following an argument.<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.nydailynews.com/sports/indiana-pacers-chris-copeland-stabbed-nyc-club-article-1.2177265|title=Indiana Pacers forward Chris Copeland stabbed at 1 OAK club; two Atlanta Hawks arrested in aftermath: NYPD sources|first=Rocco |last=Parascandola|work=[[Daily News (New York)|New York Daily News]]|date=April 8, 2015|access-date=April 8, 2015}}</ref> During the altercation, the NYPD officers broke Sefolosha's right leg, shutting him down for the rest of the season.<ref>{{cite news|last1=Arnovitz|first1=Kevin|title=Hawks' Thabo Sefolosha has broken leg, out for season|url=https://www.espn.com/nba/story/_/id/12656394/atlanta-hawks-forward-thabo-sefolosha-broken-leg-indefinitely|access-date=9 October 2015|work=[[ESPN]]|date=10 April 2015}}</ref> He underwent surgery on April 16, to repair a fractured tibia and ligament damage.<ref>{{cite news|title=Hawks' Sefolosha undergoes surgery for injured right leg|url=http://www.nba.com/2015/news/04/17/atlanta-hawks-thabo-sefolosha-undergoes-surgery.ap/|access-date=9 October 2015|work=NBA.com|date=17 April 2015}}</ref>

The prosecution offered Sefolosha a [[plea bargain]], which would have involved a dismissal of the charges after six months, but Sefolosha refused it on 9 September 2015, even though his attorney, [[Alex Spiro]], urged him to take it.<ref>{{cite web|title=A Wrongful-Arrest Defense Clinic: The Thabo Sefolosha Story|first=David |last=Lat|work=Above The Law|date=March 23, 2016|access-date=August 20, 2018|url=https://abovethelaw.com/2016/03/a-wrongful-arrest-defense-clinic-the-thabo-sefolosha-story/}}</ref> Sefolosha said that he wanted to let the case proceed to trial instead; at the same time, charges against Antić were dropped.<ref>{{Cite news|url=https://www.nytimes.com/2015/09/10/nyregion/thabo-sefolosha-atlanta-hawks-player-refuses-plea-bargain.html?_r=0 |title=Thabo Sefolosha, Atlanta Hawks Player, Spurns Lenient Plea Bargain|newspaper=The New York Times|date=2015-09-09|last1=Mckinley|first1=James C. Jr.}}</ref> Sefolosha's court hearing was set on 5 October.<ref>{{cite news|last1=Buhler|first1=John|title=Thabo Sefolosha's Court Date Set, Antic's Charges Dropped|url=http://atlallday.com/2015/09/09/thabo-sefoloshas-court-date-set-antics-charges-dropped/|access-date=9 September 2015|work=atlallday.com|date=9 September 2015}}</ref> Four days later, a [[New York City Criminal Court|Manhattan]] jury found him not guilty of all three misdemeanor charges: [[obstructing government administration]], [[disorderly conduct]] and [[resisting arrest]].<ref>{{cite news|title=Hawks' Thabo Sefolosha found not guilty in NYC arrest case|url=https://www.espn.com/nba/story/_/id/13843715/atlanta-hawks-thabo-sefolosha-found-not-guilty-nyc-arrest-case|access-date=9 October 2015|work=[[ESPN]]|agency=Associated Press|date=9 October 2015}}</ref> On 21 October, Sefolosha announced that he would be suing the city of New York as well as eight police officers for up to $50 million in damages.<ref>{{cite web|last1=Rosenberg|first1=Rebecca|last2=Marsh|first2=Julia|title=NBAer who beat charges in melee outside club to sue NYC for up to $50M|url=https://nypost.com/2015/10/21/nbaer-plans-50m-lawsuit-against-city-over-broken-leg/|work=NYPost.com|date=October 21, 2015|access-date=October 21, 2015}}</ref> On 9 April 2017, it was announced Sefolosha had settled with the NYPD for $4 million, a "substantial portion" of which he donated to [[Gideon's Promise]], a nonprofit organization dedicated to educating [[public defender (United States)|public defenders]].<ref>{{Cite news|url=http://www.espn.com/nba/story/_/id/19104575/thabo-sefolosha-atlanta-hawks-donate-part-4-million-settlement-legal-nonprofit|title=Sefolosha will give part of $4M to legal charity|work=ESPN.com|access-date=2017-04-09}}</ref>

In October 2017, Sefolosha revealed that he saved a woman the previous month from drowning while he and his family were on a rafting trip down the [[Provo River]].<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.espn.com/nba/story/_/id/20949610/utah-jazz-forward-thabo-sefolosha-rescues-woman-provo-river-raft-trip|title=Utah Jazz F Thabo Sefolosha rescues woman on Provo River trip|work=ESPN.com|date=October 7, 2017|access-date=January 14, 2018}}</ref>
